svg.title: ExplainSQL on a slow query: the verdict, the slowest node, why the planner uses no index, and the suggested index tested with HypoPG
svg.desc: Recorded from a real run of explainsql 0.1.0 against PostgreSQL 16.14.

g.text: The query: a customer's order summary
SELECT c.name, count(*) AS orders, sum(o.amount) AS total
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
Enter EXPLAIN ANALYZE on PostgreSQL 16.14, rolled back
13.4 ms. 99% of it in Seq Scan on orders o, which reads 200,000 rows to keep 10.
Planning 0.074 ms · Execution 13.4 ms · Buffers 2,517 pages, 100% from cache

Why does Seq Scan on orders o not use an index?
No index can serve the condition of Seq Scan on orders o: even with sequential scans off, the planner
no index on orders starts with customer_id
Create an index that serves the condition: see the advice.
Planned again with enable_seqscan = off; estimated.

On Seq Scan on orders o
An index on orders (customer_id) would let Seq Scan on orders o read only the rows it keeps instead of
Building it reads all of orders (27.9 MB with its indexes). CONCURRENTLY does not block writes, but
takes longer and cannot run inside a transaction.
